back: The release of harmful substances or energy into the environment faster than it can disperse, break down or absorb them.
Reduce → reuse → recycle → recover energy or compost → dispose (landfill) as the last resort.
Lined site where waste is compacted and covered with soil daily; leachate and gas are controlled. An open dump has no controls.
Polluted liquid formed when rainwater drains through rotting waste; it can contaminate soil, groundwater and streams.
Water, air, land, noise and visual (graffiti). Give a source, a pollutant and an effect for each.
Social (disease, stress), economic (treatment and health costs, lost tourism), physical (eutrophication, contaminated soil, flooding).
In 2017 Zimbabwe banned expanded polystyrene (kaylite) food containers, a major source of litter.
Outbreak in Harare, Chitungwiza and elsewhere caused about 4,000 deaths; burst sewers, broken water supply and uncollected refuse helped it spread.
Laws and fines (EMA, polluter pays), treatment at source, bans, education and clean-ups, zoning of industry.
